title: How to take antibiotics correctly
what: Antibiotics kill bacteria. They do not work on viruses, such as colds and flu.
why: When a doctor found a bacterial infection and prescribed an antibiotic.
duration: a course usually lasts a few days; your doctor will say exactly
tell_doctor: An allergy to antibiotics, if you have had one
All your other medicines, since antibiotics can interact with them
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Prescription
prepare.text: Take only the antibiotic your doctor prescribed for this illness.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: Find out how many times a day and for how many days. Set reminders.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Some are taken before meals, some after. Read the leaflet or ask your doctor.

bring: Your prescription or the doctor's instructions
A list of your other medicines
steps: Take the antibiotic at the same times each day
Take it for as many days as your doctor said
Do not stop the course on your own, even if you feel better
If you miss a dose, do not take a double one: ask your doctor or read the leaflet
Do not keep leftovers for later or give them to anyone
feel: You usually feel better in 2 to 3 days
Sometimes you get an upset stomach or nausea
after: If you are no better after 2 to 3 days, tell your doctor
Ask your doctor whether you need probiotics
red_flags: Swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing: call emergency services
A rash all over or blisters: see a doctor urgently
Frequent watery stools with blood: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: Do I need an antibiotic for a cold?
faq.a: Usually not. A cold is a virus. Your doctor decides.

faq.q: Can I stop the course if I feel better?
faq.a: No, not on your own. The infection can come back. Ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Time for your antibiotic. Plain water, on schedule.
